edits.old_latex: The AC registry excludes $C_q$, $U_{1.25}$, and their exposure-capped witnesses. edits.new_latex: A new participant-level constant-power-factor evaluation sets $C_Q=C_P^{\rm final}$ as a declared common-embedding assumption, while preserving the historical two-map model as a separate sensitivity. At the original 18 hours, three states and three power factors, rolling M2, $U_{1.25}$, $C_q$ and retrospective $x^{\rm EC}$ give 648 records per mapping. All converge; under the common map, thermal passes are 84, 66, 78 and 66 of 162, respectively, with a maximum loading of 278.40\%. All pass the declared voltage and simple reactive-bound checks. Mapping changes do not alter paired ordering or feasibility classifications at the stated tolerances. These selected fixed-injection checks do not establish annual security. The balancing key has no identified generator-specific allocation; a fleet-only aggregate diagnostic fails in part because some balancing buses contain no device in the inventoried native generator/interchange fleet. Other load or renewable allocations remain outside that conditional test.
edits.reason: Distinguish new common-map results, historical sensitivity and conditional headroom limits; preserve adverse thermal findings.

edits.new_latex: These results concern synthetic transport nominations, an hourly deterministic DC evaluator with fixed counter-injections, and penalized overloads. The system-level conclusion is that debit definitions change feasible operating choices and customer exposure associated with network relief. edits.old_latex: The AC registry contains $18\cdot3\cdot13\cdot3=2{,}106$ power-flow records. All converge and pass the stated voltage/reactive checks, but only 846 pass thermal limits. Among 162 records per named variant, thermal passes are 162 for background, zero for unrestricted requests, 48 for rolling M1, and 84 for rolling M2. The registry-wide maximum loading is 292.45\%, not a premium or annual-M2 maximum. Of 324 normalized-index comparisons, 270 are DC ties and all 54 others preserve ordering. This does not establish annual unnormalized-objective ordering or yearlong AC security.
